payload.task_text:
I need your help putting together an enrollment trend analysis for our capacity planning meeting next week. We have course and enrollment records in our learning management system going back a couple of years and I want to understand how enrollment has shifted across semesters so we can forecast what to expect and plan accordingly.

There is a capacity planning guide in the workspace called Capacity_Planning.pdf that lays out our thresholds and methodology. Please read through it first so you understand the rules we use for determining when a course section needs to be split, when we should consider consolidating, how we calculate growth trends, and what our faculty staffing ratios are.

Pull all the course and enrollment data from the learning management system. Each course name includes the semester and year in parentheses, like "Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2013)". The course code also encodes this with a suffix where J means Fall and B means Spring. I need you to group things by the base course name (without the semester/year part) so we can see trends over time.

Create an Excel file called Enrollment_Analysis.xlsx in the workspace with three sheets. The first sheet should be called "Enrollment Trends" with columns Course_Base_Name, Semester, Year, and Student_Count (the number of students enrolled in that offering). Include one row per course offering, sorted by Course_Base_Name alphabetically, then by Year, then by Semester with Spring before Fall within the same year.

The second sheet should be called "Course Capacity" with columns Course_Base_Name (sorted alphabetically), Latest_Enrollment (the student count from the most recent offering), Growth_Trend (Increasing if the latest is more than 5 percent above the immediately previous offering in chronological order, Decreasing if more than 5 percent below it, otherwise Stable; if only one offering exists, use Stable), Needs_Split (Yes if latest enrollment exceeds 2500), Consider_Consolidation (Yes if latest enrollment is below 500), Projected_Next (a linear regression forecast for the next offering based on all available data points, rounded to a whole number), and Faculty_Needed (the number of faculty required, computed from Projected_Next using the staffing ratios in the capacity planning guide: if Projected_Next is below 500, use 1 instructor per 30 students, otherwise use 1 instructor per 50 students; round to a whole number).

The third sheet should be called "Department Summary" with rows for the following metrics and their values: Total_Courses_Offered (count of all individual course offerings), Total_Student_Enrollments (sum of all student counts across all offerings), Avg_Enrollment_Per_Course (rounded to a whole number), Courses_Needing_Split, Courses_To_Consolidate, and Total_Projected_Enrollment (sum of all projected values, rounded to a whole number).

Also create a Google Form called "Course Preference Survey" so we can gauge student interest for next semester. It should have four questions. First, a short text question asking for the student's full name. Second, a checkbox question listing all the base course names as options so students can select which courses they are interested in taking. Third, a radio button question for preferred schedule with three options: Morning, Afternoon, and Evening. Fourth, a short text question asking if they have any accessibility needs or special accommodations.

Finally, send an email to each of the seven department chairs with the course enrollment projections for the courses in their department. Each base course maps to a department and its chair as follows: Applied Analytics & Algorithms belongs to the Analytics department (analytics_chair@university.edu); Biochemistry & Bioinformatics to the Biochemistry department (biochem_chair@university.edu); Creative Computing & Culture to the Computing department (computing_chair@university.edu); Data-Driven Design to the Design department (design_chair@university.edu); Environmental Economics & Ethics to the Economics department (economics_chair@university.edu); Foundations of Finance to the Finance department (finance_chair@university.edu); and Global Governance & Geopolitics to the Governance department (governance_chair@university.edu). Each email should have a subject line like "Enrollment Forecast - [Department Name]" and include the projected enrollment and faculty needs for that chair's course(s) in the body.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent must complete the task directly; do not dispatch sub-agents. Resolve the task's accessible workspace directory from the harness and use it for every relative input and output path rather than writing to a hard-coded /workspace path.

Read Capacity_Planning.pdf and guide.md first. Then call canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true), validate unique course IDs/codes/names, and issue one native-parallel batch containing exactly one canvas_get_course_grades(course_id=<literal returned ID>, page=1, per_page=1, type=["StudentEnrollment"]) call for every returned course. Student_Count is pagination.total_count; do not fetch or transmit enrollment rows. Freeze one canonical course table with {course_id, course_code, full_course_name, course_base_name, semester, year, student_count}. Reject duplicate identities or a course name/code whose semester cannot be parsed.

From that table, apply the task and guide rules exactly: chronological offering order uses year and Spring-before-Fall, Growth_Trend compares the latest and immediately previous offering with the strict five-percent thresholds, regression uses consecutive chronological indices and predicts the next index, and all split, consolidation, projection, staffing, sorting, rounding, and department-summary values must be computed once. Before writing anything, freeze one canonical payload containing the 22 offering rows, seven base-course capacity rows, six summary metrics, and seven department email facts. Every downstream output must consume those literal values without recomputation.

After the payload is frozen, start the workbook creation, create_form, and seven exact Sent-mail searches in the same native-parallel response; all three branches depend only on the canonical payload and must not wait for another branch's read-back.

- The main agent is the sole writer of Enrollment_Analysis.xlsx in the resolved workspace. Create exactly Enrollment Trends, Course Capacity, and Department Summary with the task's exact headers, row ordering, literal numeric values, and no formulas; read all populated ranges back and reconcile them with the canonical payload.
- Call create_form(title="Course Preference Survey") exactly once in this run and retain its returned formId. On that formId, sequentially add the four questions in the required order with the exact seven base-course options and schedule options, then call get_form(formId). Google Forms exposes no list/search operation: do not attempt create-or-reuse, and never retry an ambiguous create_form failure.
- For Analytics, Biochemistry, Computing, Design, Economics, Finance, and Governance, search Sent mail for the complete exact recipient and subject Enrollment Forecast - <Department Name>. Read candidate messages to verify recipients. Send only missing messages, using that department's literal projected enrollment and faculty need from the canonical payload, in one native-parallel send batch; then search/read all seven exact messages back.

Accept only after the workbook, form, and seven messages all reconcile with the same payload and no duplicate external write was made.
